Then I can’t stop thinking about it until I check and re-check the receipt, their bag, even replay the conversation in my head.

It’s like that with everything—locking up at night, counting the tills. I’ll lock the doors, but I feel this surge of panic and have to go back and pull on them several times, or recount the cash until it “feels right.” I know it’s excessive, but if I try to ignore it, the anxiety just builds until I give in.

I do get irritated and snap at my staff over small mistakes, but it’s more from this constant tension and needing everything “just so,” not from any specific incident or trauma.
